Grey Leaf

Overview

Grey Leaf speaks for the Green Clan of the Woodsfolk. He asks Zak to help their kidnapped elder Khabburu and distinguishes the clan’s arrows from the forged evidence used against them. When the clan moves, he opens its hidden route to Zak. His observations of the cloaked woman near the mines provide a crucial clue to the Princess’s imprisonment. [1, 2, 3, 4]

The arrow and the Green Clan

The arrow in the Snoop’s body appears to implicate the Woodsfolk. Sver explains that their markings identify a clan, while the governor discovers that the case containing similar arrows has been stolen from his collection. Two lines of inquiry now run alongside each other: the stolen collection and the Woodsfolk’s testimony. To approach Grey Leaf, Zak first returns the Green Clan’s Sacred Flower after rescuing its keeper from the White Clan. Grey Leaf then asks for help with the kidnapped elder Khabburu and his captor. The clan ultimately identifies the murder arrow as a false attribution, even refusing to blame its enemies for it. When the clan moves, Zak receives access to its hidden route and new home. [5, 6, 1, 2, 3, 7]

Diera and the locked mines

At the Green Clan’s new home, Grey Leaf describes the supposed man in grey as a white-haired woman. Zak identifies Diera, whose own traps protected the stolen collection. Her urgent warnings against the abandoned mines reinforce his suspicion. Tilvar explains that the governor holds the key. Karansul suggests winning it with a gold nugget and gives access to a dangerous pit, concealing the tigers that drove out its workers; Sver warns Zak of the trap. Zak obtains the nugget and presents it to the collector-governor as a business prospect. Valrasian releases the mine key, opening the way past Diera’s mercenaries. [4, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14]
